task_reviews.manual_comparison: All eight ordinary case cells agree; singular-only personal/common and neuter series, hwǣm selected and hwām recognized, no invented plural/feminine.
All twelve requested hwilc cells agree, including feminine plural hwilca and zero neuter plural hwilc.
Both requested four-part systems agree: hwæðerne/hwæðerre/hwæðer/hwæðerra and hūlicne/hūlicre/hūlic/hūlicra. Syncope and zero cells not copied from ōðer.
Complete requested masculine singular and neuter plural ilca agree; weak-only, with plural -ra/-um explicitly distinguished from -an.
Strong/weak nominative triples, selfne and all-gender selfum agree. No compulsory article rule is invented for weak self.
All sixteen requested grouped answers agree: sumu and ǣnigu versus gehwilc/swilc zero. The full gender coverage of dative plural is explicit.
All eight līf cells agree; the object in our lives is a contextual individual-life plural, not an inferred abstract-plural rule.
All twelve indicative and twelve logical subjunctive cells agree, including ætēowast, -iað, -odon and present -ien versus past -oden.
All twelve logical scīnan subjunctive cells and both geblētsian commands agree; present ī contrasts with past i, and addressee number controls commands.
All three finite-first questions preserve the original subject agreement and tense; no auxiliary dōn is added.
The subject hwā and objects hwone/hwæt agree with the independent solution; object function determines case.
Dative recipient hwǣm and genitive possessor hwæs agree; the possessed ship remains accusative object.
Attributive singular hwæðer has the supplied two-man context; predicative hūlic agrees with neuter scip. No new partitive phrase is required.
How and why remain distinct invariant lexical questions; swimð stays third singular and general instrumental syntax is not assumed.
Ǣnigne fisc is the requested masculine accusative singular. A plural noun answer would miss the express target; English do supplies no OE auxiliary.
Singular sum mann/hæfð/scip and plural sume męnn/habbað/scipu all agree. The key correctly avoids inventing a one-ship-per-man distribution.
Both singular gehwilc subjects take siehð; a weak noun does not force weak inflection of this pronoun adjective.
Both ōðer forms agree; other/another is distinct from the earlier ordinal sense, and morphology remains strong after the article.
Accusative ðone ilcan mann and dative ðǣm ilcan męnn agree; homographic ilcan does not erase the other words’ case.
Hē self gives subject emphasis; nęrie mē selfne gives the expressly male reflexive accusative. The key separates government from English myself.
Inflected nominative masculine plural swilce modifies men; it is not the homographic invariant likewise adverb.
All four phrases agree, including dative singular ǣnigum gefēran, weak ilce, and strong masculine accusative plural lȳtle after swilce.
The relative subject is ðe; its finite verb has the ship as object. Main subject remains the man.
The main clause remains I saw; relative ðe is the object of has and se mann its subject.
Dative external recipient and nominative internal subject se are correctly distinguished; helpan governs dative mē.
Accusative external object and dative internal person helped are correctly distinguished; the key enforces the expressly selected ordinary pattern.
Second-singular hulpe and singular imperative sęle agree with ðū. Both mē forms are dative, for distinct governed roles.
Plural gē/hulpon/sęllað agree, while relative ðe, first-singular mē and singular fish remain unchanged. The key correctly permits a specified dual pronoun with plural finite forms.
All three analyses agree: invariant subject, invariant object, and genitive relative ðæs as masculine singular possessor of accusative neuter scip. The genitive example is not attraction.
The always-same-case claim is rejected; ordinary internal government and the limited attested attraction exception are both retained.
Identical gefyllað serves explicitly distinguished finish and fill senses; accusative singular work contrasts with plural waters wæteru.

Both solutions use habban with accusative animals and on+dative gewealde; his is invariant and ðīnum agrees. My optional article ðā in eall ðā nīetenu is valid; the key’s articleless eall nīetenu matches the checked source frame.
Both singular and plural cognate accusatives agree, including selected ūru and plural libbað.
Indicative ætēowað versus jussive ætēowie agree; dry land is nominative subject of intransitive appear.
Model and independent answer agree. Singular-possessor Ðīn and plural-possessor Ēowru are both explicitly allowed; works and predicate gōd remain neuter plural.
My trēow is a documented spelling variant; key selected trēo is correct. Invariant his and predicate æppelbǣre agree.
The independent and key models agree: ðū eart and predicate nominative se mann.
My frozen geār misplaced the quantity mark. Selected gēar is confirmed by prior gear-nom-sg and fresh Cook Exercises p68 s.v. year; the key is correct. Frozen witness remains unchanged.
Past singular geworhte and definite masculine plural ðās lȳtlan fuglas agree; the key also permits semantically suitable gescēop.
My swilce alone is expressly accepted by the key; its reinforced ēac swilce preserves likewise without changing the grammatical function.
Nominative neuter plural ūru nīetenu, plural sēoð and singular accusative grass agree.
Both models give libbað ūru līf. Fresh source confirms the parenthetic reference is §168.1 and the cognate-accusative construction.
Plural sǣd controls weaxað; his remains invariant and on ðǣre eorðan is locative dative. All agree.
Plural animals rest themselves; hīe has the reflexive accusative function. Nīetenu and earlier dēor are valid alternatives.
Plural gefyllað and singular gefyl are both allowed because English leaves the addressee unspecified; plural waters do not decide command number.
Jussive third-singular ætēowie drȳgnes agrees and matches the checked p124 witness. The two source-proposal/canonical IDs are aliases only.
Exact supplied gesęte and local dative placement frame agree. The key admits both singular and plural fish but retains the supplied singular addressee.
Explicit singular hafa, masculine plural ealle gāstas and dative neuter singular ðīnum gewealde agree; spatial under is not substituted.
Present subjunctive third plural scīnen and dative plural location agree, with long ī; source-proposal ID reconciliation changes no form.
My sęcge and key cweðe both express I say; the key expressly accepts both. Singular/plural blessing commands remain defensible because the prompt does not fix the addressee.
Second-singular relative gescēope and imperative geblētsa agree with Thou. The key also permits prior geworhtest without losing person or meaning.
Both full translations preserve the scene, six spoken turns, three men, companion relations, plural fish versus one later fish, and final past saw.

Exactly three direct questions are identified. Key copular hwā as a possible predicate nominative is compatible with my identification analysis; it does not make accusative or a uniquely proved subject/predicate assignment mandatory.
Both analyses preserve hine as the masculine fish object, recipient ðǣm męnn, relative subject se, and helpan’s dative mē referring to the answerer.

Key selected twā lȳtlu scipu is correct. My lȳtle is explicitly a valid unselected neuter plural in the actual prior register and Cook p39; it is not an agreement error. My definite alternative ðā twā lȳtlan scipu also preserves two ships and the relative, as the key’s alternative note permits.

The full four-turn translation agrees in every event and recipient: useful to the named groups, boarding/cargo, row, sell, buy foreign goods, bring here to plural you, risk, occasional wreck/loss, barely escape alive. Collective hit is handled explicitly.
Both direct questions agree: accusative hwæt as thing said, and elliptical hū asking how useful. Address and ellipsis are supplied, not inferred productive systems.
Accusative neuter plural antecedent ðing versus nominative neuter plural relative ðā and plural passive auxiliary agree; produced remains explicitly supported.
Goods are acquired by buying and delivered here to the addressees; no manufacture, later commodity list or profit clause is added. Key preserves the syncretic-case limit of sǣ.
Risk, shipwreck and loss offer three acceptable danger expressions; barely escaping alive is accurately explained as the merchant’s accompanying circumstance.
Interrogative plural subject hwilce męnn/habbað and object ships agree; singular relative subject ðū still governs gesāwe.
Accusative another fish, dative same man and nominative relative se ðe agree; grammatical invariant-only alternatives are correctly distinguished from the required target.
Plural masculine ǣnige lȳtle fuglas and second-singular siehst agree; strong adjective environment is retained.
Singular gehwilc gefēra and strong subject emphasis self agree; finite-first transformation keeps geseah and the same participants.
Both solutions preserve the subject relative and direct quoted third-singular jussive. The key correctly allows prior sægð as an alternative reporting verb.
Determiner ðæt and inflected relative ðæt have distinct functions despite identical accusative neuter spelling; neither is a content conjunction here.

new_text_reviews.review: Finite-first yes/no, singular man as subject and ship object.
Personal nominative hwā and accusative hwone correctly contrast.
Dative recipient hwǣm and genitive possessor hwæs independently govern their questions.
Accusative thing interrogative and distinct how/why lexical adverbs.
Which, which of two, and predicative what-sort questions preserve agreement and supplied two-man context.
Some/certain singular versus some plural agrees with has/have and ship/ships.
Any fish uses singular accusative; each man remains singular.
Other/another reuses strong morphology; same uses weak nominative ilca.
Strong nominative self emphasizes hē; ship stays the object.
Inflected such in singular/plural is distinct from the earlier adverb likewise.
Invariant relative is subject; main-clause copular phrase identifies the man.
Invariant relative is object; relative noun subject has the ship.
Dative antecedent recipient versus nominative relative helper, with dative helped person.
Accusative antecedent seen versus dative relative person helped.
Second-singular hulpe and singular command sęle follow personal antecedent ðū.
Genitive relative ðæs identifies a masculine singular possessor; accusative neuter scip is the thing seen.

All 62 words and six spoken turns checked. Three men and their speaker/companion/recipient relations are coherent; three direct questions and subject/object relatives are graded through prior and new teaching. Complete independent translation compared with the key.

Barely escaping alive keeps cwic as nominative masculine singular merchant and ætberstende as supplied accompanying participle; no new passive reading.
